Subject: PrimeDocs dedicated capacity activation choreography and fallback ladder

Team —

PrimeDocs verbally committed to the dedicated capacity bundle this morning (DEAL-PRIME-8342). They want a predictable activation window and a clear fallback ladder if we need to throttle/rollback. High-level asks from them: a firm cutover window in the next three weeks, a throughput acceptance test, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Request: can infra and eng confirm a concrete GPU allocation, a minimal smoke-test matrix, and two fallback options we can present? Monica, please draft a short onboarding checklist for the CS handoff (keys, onboarding doc, support SLA).

Goal: present a single-page activation choreography to PrimeDocs by EOD tomorrow so they can align procurement.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.ai]

Subject: Re: PrimeDocs dedicated capacity activation choreography and fallback ladder

Evelyn / Ben —

Thanks — we are ready to proceed on the commitment. Procurement needs the SOW and SOC2 controls in place; we can sign the SOW once the DocuSign link is out. For cutover, our preference is the evening of Sept 20th (window 22:00–02:00 PST) so internal stakeholders are available and traffic is lower.

Acceptance criteria: 99th p99 latency for our primary model under 350ms after cutover; throughput target = 120 qps sustained (chat load). If you can present a clear rollback plan and a canary traffic plan, procurement will green-light the SOW.

I’m cc’ing ops@primedocs.ai for procurement follow-ups.

—Matt Jenkins

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-05T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrimeDocs dedicated capacity activation choreography and fallback ladder

Folks —

Quick capacity readout based on the committed bundle:
- Allocated capacity: 8x A100s (80GB) split across 2 nodes (4 GPUs/node) in us-west-2 reserved pool.
- Expected baseline: ~130 qps sustained for the curated chat model at 1.2k token context with KV caching enabled; p99 estimated 260–320ms depending on prompt distribution.

Fallback options (two-tier ladder):
1) Throttle + degrade model variant: automatically shift 25% of traffic to a quantized 8-bit variant with slightly reduced quality but ~40% lower token cost.
2) Regional fallback: mirror traffic to a secondary pool in us-west-1 with capacity reserve (warm pool) for up to 60% peak; will add ~150ms network overhead.

I've attached a capacity-matrix.csv with node allocation and a short fallback-policy.md. Both include safety thresholds and an ops-runbook snippet for rollbacks.

Constraints/notes:
- We need a 48-hour blackout for infra config changes before cutover to validate kernel selection and KV warm-up.
- If PrimeDocs requires higher sustained throughput (>=160 qps), we’ll need +4 GPUs and a short procurement lead on reserved instances.

Let me know if this matches expectations and I’ll produce the single-page activation choreography.

—Markus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-06T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrimeDocs dedicated capacity activation choreography and fallback ladder

Thanks Markus — that allocation looks good. Proposed acceptance and test plan:
- Smoke tests (pre-cutover): run synthetic traffic at 50%, 75%, 100% of target qps for 2-hour windows across two days to validate KV cache warm-up and kernel selections. Expected p95/p99 targets logged to Grafana.
- Canary (cutover): route 10% production traffic for first 30 minutes, if p99 < 350ms and error rate < 0.5% advance to 50% for 1 hour, then full.
- Rollback triggers: p99 > 500ms for 10 minutes or error rate > 1% => immediate rollback to hosted endpoints.

I'll prepare a smoke-test-windows.md with exact command lines, expected dashboards, and alert thresholds. Recommend we schedule the 48-hour config freeze starting Sept 18 at 00:00 PST to ensure kernel farms are stable.

Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
